content_of_post_to_answer: Do we miss our childhood when we grow up?
answer: We often miss childhood, but sometimes what we miss is not the age itself—it’s the feeling of having fewer responsibilities, more unstructured time, and a world that still felt larger than us. Adulthood removes some of that innocence, but it also reveals why childhood felt so effortless. I’ve explored this pattern more on my profile if you want to go deeper. Perhaps we don’t miss being children as much as we miss being less burdened.
